title: Planning's own clock
question: By the Planning Department's own measure, how often does a review step miss its deadline?
finding: Of 8,791 review steps the Planning Department has scored against a deadline, 2,868 (33%) ran over. First plan review missed its 30-day deadline 60% of the time in 2023 and 12% in 2026. From an accepted application to approval took a median 160 days for applications accepted since 2021.
how: The Planning Department's published review metrics: each row is one project at one stage, with the days taken, the deadline the Department applied and whether it scored the step over or under.
limits: Most rows carry no deadline or no score, so the share over deadline describes only the steps the Department chose to score. Deadlines come from State law (the Permit Streamlining Act and later housing laws) and from the Department's own targets; the rulebook should confirm which is which. An applicant who is slow to resubmit lengthens the whole but not the scored step.
